P4 north-west bedroom (parts/room-36.mjs): one red bed with its head on the north wall at (70,6,14), chest dresser, barrel nightstand with a standing lantern, red rug, and a desk (fence post, lit candle, stair chair) on the west side. The x71 column is kept clear as the lane from the east doorway.
In a throwaway test shell the room reads OK: 11 of 11 cells reachable from the doorway, fit OK, light min 10 with no dark cells. The real build with make.sh is whole, and this part adds no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE writes.
Deviation from plan: the bed head is on the north wall, not the west wall x69, because the west side at x68 z15..17 is the stair hole and the north wall at x68..69 holds a window pair.
left: Re-run `$MCD room build.nbt --rooms rooms.json --only "P4 north-west bedroom"` once the shell, floor y5, walls and ceiling are merged: in my copy they are absent, so the walk check reports no way in and FIT reports floating carpet, the chair and the desk, plus the bed head against an opening. The test shell I used is at /tmp/p43/test.nbt (not part of the build).
The room check's entrance is the P0 door, so in isolation the walk always fails; the doorway-based walk was verified with a temp rooms file (entrance [72,6,15]), not with the real rooms.json.
The bed head is on the north wall (70,6,14), not the plan's west wall x69. Plan Notes not edited, since parallel workers may be editing plan.md; the fact is worth a line there.
No plan.md checklist or elements.md item is specific to this room (the Parts checklist covers six parts only, and bed and lighting items are row-wide), so nothing was ticked.

waste.what: Checking walk and FIT for an upper-floor bedroom in isolation: its only entrance in rooms.json is the P0 door, so the walk always fails, and the shell is absent in my copy. I wrote a throwaway mock-shell script and a temp rooms file (entrance moved to the room's doorway) to get a meaningful verdict.
waste.cost: about 3 tool calls and two scratch files in /tmp/p43

waste.cost: about 4 coordinate calculations and two layers() calls; roughly 20 blocks placed through layers and bed()
waste.tool: A `mcd plan --furnish <room> --recipe bedroom` (or a room recipe in rooms.json) that places bed, dresser, nightstand with lantern and a desk with the lane kept clear, and reports the lane and bed-head checks before writing.

waste.what: Reading the room tool's FLOOR and LIGHT grids by eye to tell real walkability problems apart from missing-shell artefacts.
waste.cost: several re-reads of the output across two builds
waste.tool: `mcd room --only` should label each cell's cause ('no floor in this build' vs 'blocked by furniture' vs 'unreachable from the entrance') so missing neighbours are not read as design faults.

structured_output.summary:
P4 north-west bedroom (parts/room-36.mjs): one red bed with its head on the north wall at (70,6,14), chest dresser, barrel nightstand with a standing lantern, red rug, and a desk (fence post, lit candle, stair chair) on the west side. The x71 column is kept clear as the lane from the east doorway.
In a throwaway test shell the room reads OK: 11 of 11 cells reachable from the doorway, fit OK, light min 10 with no dark cells. The real build with make.sh is whole, and this part adds no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE writes.
Deviation from plan: the bed head is on the north wall, not the west wall x69, because the west side at x68 z15..17 is the stair hole and the north wall at x68..69 holds a window pair.
left: Re-run `$MCD room build.nbt --rooms rooms.json --only "P4 north-west bedroom"` once the shell, floor y5, walls and ceiling are merged: in my copy they are absent, so the walk check reports no way in and FIT reports floating carpet, the chair and the desk, plus the bed head against an opening. The test shell I used is at /tmp/p43/test.nbt (not part of the build).
The room check's entrance is the P0 door, so in isolation the walk always fails; the doorway-based walk was verified with a temp rooms file (entrance [72,6,15]), not with the real rooms.json.
The bed head is on the north wall (70,6,14), not the plan's west wall x69. Plan Notes not edited, since parallel workers may be editing plan.md; the fact is worth a line there.
No plan.md checklist or elements.md item is specific to this room (the Parts checklist covers six parts only, and bed and lighting items are row-wide), so nothing was ticked.

waste.what: Checking walk and FIT for an upper-floor bedroom in isolation: its only entrance in rooms.json is the P0 door, so the walk always fails, and the shell is absent in my copy. I wrote a throwaway mock-shell script and a temp rooms file (entrance moved to the room's doorway) to get a meaningful verdict.
waste.cost: about 3 tool calls and two scratch files in /tmp/p43
waste.tool: `mcd room --entrance x,y,z` (override the entrance for one room) and `mcd room --assume-shell` (treat the box's outside cells as walls and its floor as solid), so isolated rooms can be checked before the shell merges.

waste.what: Hand-placing the furniture grid and the light grid as two layers() calls, computing the bed's foot/head cells and the lane by hand from plan.md's doorway coordinates.
waste.cost: about 4 coordinate calculations and two layers() calls; roughly 20 blocks placed through layers and bed()
waste.tool: A `mcd plan --furnish <room> --recipe bedroom` (or a room recipe in rooms.json) that places bed, dresser, nightstand with lantern and a desk with the lane kept clear, and reports the lane and bed-head checks before writing.

waste.what: Reading the room tool's FLOOR and LIGHT grids by eye to tell real walkability problems apart from missing-shell artefacts.

waste.tool: `mcd room --only` should label each cell's cause ('no floor in this build' vs 'blocked by furniture' vs 'unreachable from the entrance') so missing neighbours are not read as design faults.
